facts.text: I'm feeling tired, weak and low on energy.
For six months.

facts.item: tiredness and weakness: what triggered it
facts.text: I can't recall anything that triggered it.

facts.item: tiredness and weakness: change during the day
facts.text: My energy level remains constant throughout the day.

facts.item: tiredness and weakness: effect on daily activities
facts.text: I don't have energy for my daily 30-minute walk with my dog.

facts.item: tiredness and weakness: effect on work
facts.text: Even at work, I'm not as energetic as I was before.
I have a poor appetite.
I have lost 8 pounds during the past 6 months.
I have a bowel movement two or three times a week. It has been like this for the past 10 years.
Recently I've noticed more foul-smelling and greasy-looking stools.
I haven't noticed any blood in my stools.
I do feel some discomfort in my stomach.
It's here, in the upper middle part of my belly.
It began four months ago.

facts.item: stomach pain: change since it started
facts.text: It has increased gradually.

facts.item: stomach pain: what it feels like
facts.text: It's a vague, deep discomfort.
It's 4 out of 10.

facts.item: stomach pain: what makes it worse
facts.text: Nothing makes it worse.

facts.item: stomach pain: what makes it better
facts.text: I feel better when I lean forward.

facts.item: stomach pain: effect of lying on the back
facts.text: It gets worse when I lie on my back.
It isn't related to what I eat.
I feel the discomfort reaching my back.
Occasionally, I feel nauseated.
I feel sad.
I don't know, really.
I haven't had thoughts of hurting myself.
I don't blame myself for anything.
I don't feel guilty.
I don't feel worthless.
I wake up unusually early in the morning.
It has been like this for the past 2 months.
I can't concentrate anymore while watching the news or playing cards with my friends.
I don't enjoy playing cards with my friends anymore.
I feel that life is boring.
I haven't had a fever.
I don't have chest pain.
I don't have a cough.
I'm not short of breath.

I haven't noticed any recent hair loss.
My skin isn't unusually dry.

I haven't had any medical conditions.
I had an appendectomy at 16 years old.
I don't have any drug allergies.
I take Tylenol.
It's not helping.
My father had diabetes.
My father died in a car accident.
My mother died of breast cancer.
I drink beer.
I typically have two beers each day and increase that to three or four on weekends.
This routine has been consistent for many years.
It helps me unwind.
Not at all. I don't use any recreational drugs.
I used to smoke, but I quit six months ago.
A pack of cigarettes a day.
For 30 years.
I felt repulsed by it, and it made me feel unwell.
I walk 30 minutes every day.
My eating habits are consistent.
I enjoy fast food.
I have sexual relations with my wife.
I was a police officer. I retired 1 year ago.

findings.name: neck examination
findings.result: Supple; no jugular venous distension; no enlarged lymph nodes.

findings.name: lung auscultation
findings.result: Clear breath sounds on both sides.

findings.name: heart examination
findings.result: Regular rate and rhythm; normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, rubs or gallops.

findings.name: abdominal examination
findings.result: Soft, not distended; abdominal discomfort increases when lying on the back; mild epigastric tenderness, with pain on palpation of the epigastric area; no rebound tenderness; bowel sounds present in all four quadrants; no enlargement of the liver or spleen.

evidence: History of smoking and eating foods that are high in fat content
Unintentional weight loss of 8 lbs over the past 6 months
Loss of interest in activities; early awakening
Decreased appetite and unintentional weight loss
Worsening epigastric discomfort that radiates to the back

other_considerations.note: Should be suspected with any epigastric pain, and many patients deny a relation to meals, but weight loss is unusual in uncomplicated ulcer disease.
Nonspecific fatigue and weakness suggest it, but abdominal pain is unusual.

source_issues: p011: the scripted answer only repeats the question ('Sharp, vague, deep, or dull?'). The quality 'vague, deep' was taken from the note HPI (f016, source ids p011 + note, flagged).
p004 says 'even at work, I am not as energetic as I was before', but p036 says he retired 1 year ago.
p004 says he has no energy for his daily 30-minute walk, but p040 says 'I walk 30 minutes every day'.

p013 says nothing makes the discomfort worse, but the SP notes and the note HPI say it increases when he lies on his back (note fact f020, flagged; the SP-simulated finding is also in the abdominal exam record x012).
Exam line e007 records a positive Murphy's sign; neither the SP notes nor the gold mention it, and it fits poorly with the gold differential. Kept as written (x013).
p016 asks about nausea or vomiting; the answer mentions only occasional nausea, so vomiting is not recorded either way.
p021 asks about falling asleep, staying asleep, and snoring; the answer addresses only early waking.
The raw sheet's Patient Description ('married with three children') is not in the parsed source fields; added to extras.acting_notes.

Gold rank 1 is headed 'Diagnosis:' without '#1'; the rank-2 history bullets are split oddly ('Loss of interest in activities; early awakening;' / 'impaired concentration; low energy'); kept as two bullets with the trailing semicolon removed.
notes: The stage direction '(points to the epigastric area)' in p009 moved to extras.acting_notes; the location is the child fact f013, in lay words.

Mood items (sadness, early waking, poor concentration, loss of enjoyment, no guilt or suicidal thoughts) are filed as symptoms (v1 hpi) with system psychiatric, because the note places them in the HPI.

'Look weak and sad and lean forward while seated' is kept as an acting note only (general demeanor, not an examination maneuver); the note's own 'looks sad' is in general appearance (x005). The two SP-simulated findings elicited on examination (epigastric pain on palpation, discomfort lying supine) are in the abdominal exam record (x012).
p018 'I don't know, really' is recorded as a present fact (he does not know why he feels sad), not as a denial.
Smoking: resolved current status (f056) with historical amount (f057), duration (f058) and reason for quitting (f059) children.
14 template answers (No, I do not.) checked against the June-2024 release: all are plain denials there; 16 facts confirmed (flags re-keyed to the v2 ids).

Conversion: the chief complaint 'Feeling tired, weak, low energy' is one parent fact (f001, aliases fatigue / low energy / weakness); duration, trigger, daily pattern and the walk and work effects (v1 f001-f005) are its children. v1 f011 (discomfort, epigastric) becomes parent f012 + location child f013; v1 f012 (onset four months ago, increased gradually) becomes onset f014 + course f015; v1 f027 (early waking for 2 months) becomes f030 + duration f031.

Conversion: v1 f039 ('Tylenol is not helping', subtype hpi) is a treatment_response child (f047) of the Tylenol medication fact (f046), because p031 does not say which complaint Tylenol is for. Its category follows the v1 subtype as CONVERSION.md says (hpi -> symptom; system general, as no complaint is named), although the parent is a medication fact; the rules do not say which category a child takes when it differs from its parent's.

Conversion: father's diabetes (f048) and cause of death (f049) stay separate facts as in v1. Alcohol (p037) is a parent (f051) with quantity, duration and reason children; diet (p041) is a parent (f061) with a 'kind of food' child (f062).
Vitals: doorway values agree with the note's 'VS: within normal limits' (e002); one record per parameter citing both, marked initial.
Harmonisation pass: f047 category medication -> medication (parent f046); scale [0, 10] added to f017; system general (sleep) for f030, f031.
